A QUICK FIELD GUIDE

Find your way through the universe.

01

Start with a complete experiment

Scenes loads a curated combination of objects, lighting, and viewpoints. Every scene can be edited.

02

Understand the geometry

Math starts with a Relativity guide, followed by Black holes, Warp, and Wormholes. Explore the equations and diagrams, with the limits of each visual model explained alongside them.

03

Build the world

Objects is a tree rooted in Space. Children orbit or belong to their parent. Use the gear to open properties and viewpoints; Space holds the background stars and nebulas. Display contains the spectrum, lensing, exposure, grid, and render quality. The shared Grid switch controls every field together.

04

Place an object, then get close

Objects → Add an object places individual bodies. Select it in Objects to edit its physical size and placement. Near a black hole, edit the orbit’s radius, height, and phase; in open space, use local positions in meters. Craft keep their true dimensions, so choose Track to see a tiny object up close.

Track follows a close-up camera around that body. Ride · 360° looks out from it; the NASA Shuttle uses its flight deck. Choose Camera → Orbit to orbit a target, or Reset scene view to restore the scene’s starting viewpoint.

Take the helm: select the Enterprise or NASA Shuttle and choose Drive in its properties or Camera. Drive centers the selected vehicle in an orbit view. W / S changes warp factor or Shuttle acceleration; A / D changes heading. The heading slider sits above the warp slider or forward-only 0–10g acceleration slider (0.5g steps, 1g nominal). Turns settle smoothly at the chosen heading. Stop motion slows the Enterprise. For the Shuttle, Cut thrust stops the burn and leaves it coasting; turn 180° and burn to slow down. The camera icon offers Chase or Ride; Resume orbit or Esc hands control back to the simulation. Enterprise bubble radius follows its warp factor automatically. Bridge: open Space properties to edit both skies; select the traveler to choose the Enterprise, NASA Shuttle, or astronaut.

05

Choose how you observe

Map opens a diagram of the object hierarchy. Select a body to edit its orbit, open Properties, Track, or Ride. Double-click or double-tap a body to explore its children, or use the Explore children button. Use Parent and the breadcrumb trail to go back up. Camera gives you Orbit, Ride, and Free roam; spacecraft also offer Chase. In Free roam, drag to choose a heading and scroll or pinch to travel. Track or ride any physical target from the same menu. VR uses a compatible headset and WebXR browser. Every control stays available when the viewing panel is expanded.

Choose how you render. Adaptive selects the same Low, Medium, and High modes available in the menu. It steps down below 30 FPS and checks whether it can step up again. The current mode is shown beside the frame rate. Ultra is always manual: choose it for maximum detail, pause at a view you like, then use Picture → Quick to capture the live frame. A slow Ultra frame is expected on less powerful GPUs. Picture renders a separate high-resolution still in small tiles, with progress, cancellation, and a downloadable result.

MouseDrag to orbit · wheel to zoom · middle-drag to look
TouchChoose Orbit, Ride, Chase, or Free roam · drag to look or orbit · pinch to zoom or travel
KeyboardArrow keys to orbit · Shift + arrows to look · + / − to zoom · W / S to travel in Free roam

Use Labels to identify objects and horizons. Double-click or double-tap a body or label to track it; repeat on the tracked object to open its properties. Single taps, drags, and pinches do not select. Geometry in Display enables labels, the spacetime grid, and spherical grids on stars and planets, while retaining visible-light black-hole and white-hole optics. Everything needed to run is included locally.
